title: To Thee, Our God, We Fly
description: To Thee, Our God, We Fly in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Walsham How wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 304.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: To Thee, our God, we fly For mer-cy and for grace; Oh, hear our low-ly cry And hide not Thou Thy face! O Lord, stretch forth Thy might-y hand And guard and bless our Fa-ther-land.

lines: To Thee, our God, we fly
For mercy and for grace;
Oh, hear our lowly cry
And hide not Thou Thy face!
O Lord, stretch forth Thy mighty hand
And guard and bless our Fatherland.
Arise, O Lord of hosts,
Be jealous for Thy name,
And drive from out our coasts
The sins that put to shame.
O Lord, stretch forth Thy mighty hand
And guard and bless our Fatherland.
Thy best gifts from on high
In rich abundance pour
That we may magnify
And praise Thee more and more.
O Lord, stretch forth Thy mighty hand
And guard and bless our Fatherland.
The powers ordained by Thee
With heavenly wisdom bless;
May they Thy servants be
And rule in righteousness.
O Lord, stretch forth Thy mighty hand
And guard and bless our Fatherland.
The Church of Thy dear Son
Inflame with love’s pure fire;
Bind her once more in one
And life and truth inspire.
O Lord, stretch forth Thy mighty hand
And guard and bless our Fatherland.

licence: Public domain: William Walsham How died in 1897.
credits: Words by William Walsham How (1823–1897), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
